body:
I audited F3.5 against plan/08 F3.5, plan/09 §3–§5/§8/§10, plan/10, plan/03 (F28/F31/F26/F05), plan/04 §8 and plan/07. `deno task check` and `deno task publish:dry` pass; `deno check`/`deno run` on `examples/ts/main.ts` pass; the prebuilt `target/debug/rich-editor-auy-cli` was exercised with doc and envelope input; `cargo package --list` was used. No builds were triggered; `composer`/`php` are unavailable on this host (DIVERGENCES I).

FINDINGS

F1 — P0 — Published `@rich-editor-auy/dom` cannot resolve `@rich-editor-auy/core`
file: packages/ts/packages/dom/deno.json:5-6 (confidence 0.85)
The package's published deno.json ships `"imports": {"@rich-editor-auy/core": "../core/mod.ts"}`. `deno publish --dry-run` lists only `dom/deno.json`, `dom/mod.ts`, `dom/render.ts`, `dom/LICENSE`, so `../core/mod.ts` points outside the published package. I copied exactly those files to an isolated directory and `deno check mod.ts` failed with `Cannot find module 'file:///tmp/core/mod.ts'`. On JSR the same relative URL becomes an un-versioned `https://jsr.io/@rich-editor-auy/core/mod.ts` (404). Additionally the package has no `compilerOptions.lib`, so a consumer without `lib: ["dom"]` gets `Cannot find name 'HTMLElement'` (Deno 2.9's default lib omits DOM; verified). This contradicts F31 ("publicação é gate") and the F3.5 acceptance that each package is consumable; the local workspace masks it.
Minimal fix: `"imports": {"@rich-editor-auy/core": "jsr:@rich-editor-auy/core@^0.1.0"}` and add `"compilerOptions": {"lib": ["dom", "dom.iterable"]}`. I verified a `jsr:` specifier resolves to the sibling workspace member offline and passes `deno publish --dry-run`.

F2 — P1 — `fromEnvelope` ignores the envelope and re-serializes in JS; no WASM envelope API exists
file: packages/ts/packages/core/mod.ts:64-73 (confidence 0.95)
`Document.fromEnvelope(_schema, bytes)` does `JSON.parse`, pulls `.doc`, then `JSON.stringify(parsed.doc)` and calls `canonicalize`. Runtime check: an envelope with `format:"other", version:7` and a wrong `schema_fingerprint` is accepted silently. This violates plan/04 §8.2 ("`schema_fingerprint` … detecta schema errado antes de tentar carregar"), plan/09 §3.4 and F28 ("bytes canônicos são preservados, não resserializados"). The WASM crate exposes no envelope operation at all (crates/rich-editor-auy-wasm/src/lib.rs exports only 11 functions; `Envelope`/`doc_id` never cross the boundary), so a TS consumer cannot produce the durable envelope either — plan/09 §12 ("Persisto Envelope.bytes()") is unachievable. The core already has `wire::Envelope::from_json` (verifies format/version/fingerprint) and `to_json_string`.
Minimal fix: add `from_envelope`/`to_envelope` exports in the wasm crate that delegate to `Envelope::{from_json,to_json_string}`, and have `Document.fromEnvelope` call `from_envelope` with the original bytes instead of parsing JSON.

F3 — P1 — PHP `Validator` feeds envelope bytes to a CLI that only accepts a bare doc
file: cli/src/main.rs:35-45 and packages/php/src/Validator.php:24 (confidence 0.95)
`Document::fromBytes` requires and preserves an envelope, so `Document::bytes()` is envelope JSON. `Validator::validate($doc->bytes())` writes those bytes to `rich-editor-auy-cli validate`, which calls `wire::from_json` (doc parser). I ran the prebuilt binary: the envelope input gives `error: missing_type at 0 ()`, exit 1; the same doc without the envelope gives `ok`. There is no envelope path in the CLI, so the documented plan/09 §4 flow fails 100% of the time and the PHP test suite doesn't cover it.
Minimal fix: in the CLI, detect `"format":"rich-editor-auy"` and dispatch to `wire::Envelope::from_json` (which also enforces `schema_fingerprint`) for `validate`/`format`/`a11y*`/`diff`.

F4 — P1 — Schema presets are a second, inert definition; no schema ever reaches Rust
file: packages/ts/packages/schema/mod.ts:1-22 (confidence 0.9)
`basicSchema()` returns `{name, nodes:[...]}` — no marks, no attrs, no content expressions — and `documentSchema()` returns `basicSchema()`. Nothing consumes it: `EditorState.fromEnvelope(schema: unknown, …)` and `Document.fromEnvelope(_schema, …)` ignore the argument, and every wasm export hardcodes `Schema::basic()` (crates/rich-editor-auy-wasm/src/lib.rs:29,36,44,107,132). `Schema` has no JSON serialization in the core (`grep` for `to_json/from_json` under `schema/` finds none), so the plan/09 §3.1 serializer and D59 ("presets em TS emitem JSON; Rust valida") cannot work, and `SchemaError` can never surface through `init`/`fromJSON`. This is exactly the second-source-of-truth that F28 forbids, and it also makes all table/media/quote/code mappings in the adapter unreachable through the shipped artifact.
Minimal fix: add canonical schema JSON to the core + a wasm `init(schema_json)`/`schema_json()` (or a `create_state(schema_json, doc_json)`), have the TS package emit that JSON, and reject invalid schemas in Rust; otherwise record a new DIVERGENCES entry and remove the misleading preset API.

F5 — P1 — `toggle_mark` adds marks; it never toggles and cannot carry mark attributes
file: crates/rich-editor-auy-wasm/src/lib.rs:104-118 (confidence 0.95)
The doc comment says "Toggles", but the implementation always calls `Transaction::add_mark`. Runtime check: `d.toggleMark(1,5,"strong")` twice yields the same JSON as once, so a bold button can never unbold. Core has `command::toggle_mark` (crates/rich-editor-auy/src/command/mod.rs:50) which does the right thing. Second defect: the signature only takes a mark name, while the basic schema's `link`/`ref` marks have required attributes; `toggleMark(1,5,"link")` returns `{"type":"link"}` with no `href`, which the adapter then renders as an `<a>` with no href. This is reachable with `Schema::basic()`.
Minimal fix: take the mark existence from the doc/selection (or add a `remove` flag) and accept optional attrs JSON (`href`, `target`) so `link`/`ref` are constructible; use `command::toggle_mark` semantics.

F6 — P2 — Adapter is semantically poorer than the tree: `ref` marks dropped, unknown roles silently downgraded, `custom` invented
file: packages/ts/packages/dom/render.ts:43-64 and 66-113,138-140 (confidence 0.95)
plan/10 §5 hard rule: "o adaptador não pode criar um documento semanticamente mais pobre que a `A11yTree` … não emite `div` genérico em silêncio". `MARK_TAGS` (lines 8-18) has no `ref`, and line 49 `continue`s, so a document with the basic-schema `ref` mark renders the text with the mark gone (proven: `a11y_tree` returns `marks:["ref"]` while the renderer emits a bare text node). `createElement`'s `default` returns a bare `<div>` with no role, and `custom` gets `role="group"`, inventing a role instead of failing (lines 110-111, 138-139).
Minimal fix: add an explicit `ref` mapping (e.g. an element carrying `data-auy-mark="ref"` and the target, or fail), and throw/report for an unmapped role/`custom` rather than emitting `div`/inventing `group`.

F7 — P2 — Mount overrides host accessibility state and `destroy()` does not restore it
file: packages/ts/packages/dom/mod.ts:46-52,63-73 (confidence 0.9)
`render()` unconditionally does `host.setAttribute("aria-label", options.label ?? "Document")`: it replaces a consumer-provided `aria-label` during mount and `destroy()` unconditionally `removeAttribute("aria-label")` (line 71), losing it. A consumer `data-auy-root` is likewise deleted (line 72). It also only writes `lang`/`dir` when the tree has them (lines 49-50), so one `dispatch()` with a doc lacking `lang` leaves the previous `lang`/`dir` on the host (wrong language/direction announced). `destroy()` restores `innerHTML` by re-parsing (line 65), so node identity and consumer listeners on the original children are not restored — plan/09 F26/acceptance says "destroy() restaura". Also missing: `aria-readonly="true"` when `editable:false` (line 39-42), `aria-invalid`, and `aria-live` error/remote announcements required by plan/09 §8.1-8.2.
Minimal fix: save/restore `aria-label` and `data-auy-root` alongside the other attributes; set `aria-label` only when `options.label` is provided (never a hardcoded English "Document"); `removeAttribute` `lang`/`dir` when the tree lacks them; set `aria-readonly` from `editable`.

F8 — P2 — Errors cross the TS boundary as opaque strings; `AuyError` lacks `path`/`offset`; `DocumentError` is dead
file: packages/ts/packages/core/mod.ts:15-18,43-51,60-62 (confidence 0.95)
The wasm boundary maps every error through `JsValue::from_str(&Display)` (crates/rich-editor-auy-wasm/src/lib.rs:146-148), so `throw` carries a JS string. Verified: `Document.fromJSON("{bad")` throws `typeof "string"`, `[object String]`, `"expected_string at offset 1"`; `insertText(999,…)` throws `"unsupported step: text_range"`. `ParseError::Display` is only `code at offset N` (crates/rich-editor-auy/src/error/wire.rs:31) and `StepError::Display` has no code/offset (step.rs:44-61), so `path`/`offset` are unrecoverable. plan/09 §3.4 requires `AuyError` with `code`, `path`, `offset` and "nada de erro opaco"; the `AuyError` interface here has only `code`/`message`, and `DocumentError` is used only for `missing_doc`.
Minimal fix: return a structured `JsValue` (object with `code`, `path`, `offset`, `message`) from the wasm crate and have `core/mod.ts` catch and rethrow `DocumentError` with those fields.

F9 — P2 — `bind` is an alias of `mount`; `neutral`/render-data view are documented but absent
file: packages/ts/packages/dom/mod.ts:28-90 (confidence 0.9)
`bind` calls `mount` (lines 87-90), so a consumer using it with a pre-rendered, consumer-mapped DOM has that DOM replaced by `renderTree` — the opposite of D52/F26 ("`bind` transfere a responsabilidade explicitamente"). `MountOptions` has no `semantics`/`neutral` (README.md:93, plan/09 §3.3), and `view()` returns the host element (line 74) while plan/09 §3.2 defines it as render data (blocks, runs, ranges, selection) so a consumer can render it themselves. `data-auy-pos-*` from plan/09 §5.3 is not emitted either (`data-auy-from`/`to` are, render.ts:118-120). DIVERGENCES K only acknowledges the missing selection/IME/clipboard conversion, not these.
Minimal fix: implement `bind` as a non-rendering mode, implement or remove `neutral` from README/plan, and return a typed render-data view (or document the element view and record the divergence).

F10 — P2 — PHP API diverges from the documented sample; CLI offers no schema input
file: packages/php/src/Validator.php:7-33 (confidence 0.95)
plan/09 §4 shows `(new Validator($bin))->withSchema($schemaPath)->validate($doc->bytes())`; there is no `withSchema` method, and `cli/src/main.rs` has no `--schema` flag. The same plan text says the validator returns "violações, offsets"; the implementation returns the raw `{exit,stdout,stderr}` array. Since the CLI hardcodes `Schema::basic()`, validation against any other schema is impossible end-to-end (see F4).
Minimal fix: either add `withSchema()` while CLI gains a schema-file argument and the core gains schema JSON, or align plan/09 and the PHP docblock with the implemented API and record the divergence.

F11 — P2 — PHPStan level max will reject the untyped `array` declarations
file: packages/php/src/Document.php:11,40 and packages/php/src/Envelope.php:13 (confidence 0.7)
`phpstan.neon` sets `level: max`, which enables `missingType.iterableValue`. `private readonly array $json`, `public function json(): array` and `public readonly array $doc` declare no key/value types, so `vendor/bin/phpstan analyse` (CI job, plan/07) reports them. `composer`/`php` are absent here, so this wasn't executed; the rule is deterministic for level 6+.
Minimal fix: `array<string, mixed>` (or `@phpstan-type EnvelopeJson array{format:string,version:int,schema_fingerprint:string,doc:array<string,mixed>}`) on those declarations.

F12 — P2 — `make check-ecosystem` silently skips the WASM build and the PHP test/analysis gates
file: Makefile:41-43 (confidence 0.95)
plan/07 (§6, lines 473-516) defines `check-ecosystem: wasm js php`, with the PHP target running `composer install`, `validate`, `audit`, `phpunit` and `phpstan`. The Makefile only runs `deno task check/publish:dry` and `composer validate/audit`; it never builds the wasm artifact nor runs PHPUnit/PHPStan, so a stale artifact or a failing PHP test passes `make check-ecosystem` locally. AGENTS.md §7 likewise advertises "composer validate/audit/test".
Minimal fix: make `check-ecosystem` depend on `wasm js php` and have the PHP branch run `composer test`/`phpstan analyse` when composer is present.

F13 — P2 — Published Rust crates contain no LICENSE files despite listing them
file: crates/rich-editor-auy/Cargo.toml:14 (same at crates/rich-editor-auy-macros/Cargo.toml:14 and crates/rich-editor-auy-wasm/Cargo.toml:14) (confidence 0.95)
`include` lists `LICENSE-MIT`/`LICENSE-APACHE`, but those files exist only at the workspace root. `cargo package -p rich-editor-auy --list` and `-p rich-editor-auy-wasm --list` show `README.md` (copied from `../../`) but no license files. F05 requires both licenses in each published crate; the SPDX `license` field does not ship the texts.
Minimal fix: copy `LICENSE-MIT`/`LICENSE-APACHE` into each published crate (or add them via a symlink/`license-file` that cargo will package).

F14 — P2 — The WASM checksum deliverable is never produced or shipped
file: scripts/build_wasm.sh:13-15 and packages/ts/packages/core/deno.json:11 (confidence 0.9)
The plan's F3.5 deliverable requires a checksum of the artifact, and the JSR include list names `wasm/*.blake3`. The script writes it only when `b3sum` is installed (not installed here; no `.blake3` exists in `packages/ts/packages/core/wasm/`). The dry run ships no checksum, so the "artefato reprodutível" gate has nothing to compare. DIVERGENCES M records only the missing `wasm-opt`.
Minimal fix: compute the checksum with the existing BLAKE3 dependency (or make `b3sum` a required CI tool), commit/ship the file, and fail the wasm job when it is missing.

F15 — P2 — Acceptance-critical adapter behaviour has no test
file: packages/ts/packages/dom/mod_test.ts:4-6 (confidence 0.9)
The only `mount` test asserts `typeof mount === "function"` (and its name, "mount refuses without a state", is false). There is no test for `destroy()` restoration, the host `aria-label`/`lang`/`dir` handling, `aria-readonly`, or a DOM snapshot proving no `<style>`/`style=`/`class=`/`insertRule` from `mount` (plan/09 §10.1 explicitly requires the snapshot and the restore). `core/mod_test.ts` has no envelope, error-type or toggle-idempotency test, which is why F2/F5/F7 went unnoticed.
Minimal fix: add a fake-DOM mount/destroy test asserting exact attribute and child restoration, a `ref`-mark render test, an envelope-rejection test, and a double-toggle test.

F16 — P2 — The host example cannot run in a browser as written
file: examples/host/index.html:12-18 (confidence 0.8)
It loads `../../packages/ts/packages/core/mod.ts` and `.../dom/mod.ts` from a `<script type="module">`. Browsers cannot parse TypeScript (interfaces, annotations, `#private` declarations appear in these files), and there is no build/transpile or serve task anywhere in `Makefile`/`examples/README.md`; `make examples` only checks/runs `examples/ts/main.ts`. F3.5 requires a runnable host example with consumer CSS and axe-core coverage.
Minimal fix: add a documented serve/build step (e.g. `deno bundle`/import-map + generated `.js`) or point the example at compiled output, and wire it into `make examples`.

F17 — P2 — Table `scope` values are passed through in a non-HTML spelling
file: packages/ts/packages/dom/render.ts:131 (confidence 0.8)
The A11yTree JSON serializes `CellScope::ColGroup`/`RowGroup` as `"col_group"`/`"row_group"` (crates/rich-editor-auy/src/a11y/json.rs:129-136), while valid HTML `scope` tokens are `col`, `row`, `colgroup`, `rowgroup`. `applyAttributes` writes the JSON value verbatim, so a `col_group` cell emits `scope="col_group"`, which assistive tech ignores. (Reachability requires a table schema; `Schema::basic()` has none, but the adapter is the general A11yTree consumer.)
Minimal fix: translate the tree token to the HTML token (`col_group` → `colgroup`, `row_group` → `rowgroup`) or fix the JSON names to the HTML spelling.

Overall correctness: incorrect.

EXPLICIT ANSWERS

1) Matching TS declarations: yes. All 11 `#[wasm_bindgen]` exports (`version`, `schema_fingerprint`, `canonicalize`, `plain_text`, `insert_text`, `validate_a11y`, `a11y_tree`, `split_block`, `delete_range`, `toggle_mark`, `join_backward`) plus `initSync`/default are declared in `packages/ts/packages/core/wasm/rich_editor_auy_wasm.d.ts`, and `core/mod.ts` imports each one (or wraps it in `Document`). No drift found in the declaration↔export mapping; the problems are semantic (F2, F4, F5), not missing declarations.

2) DOM adapter semantics/restore: no. Semantics: `ref` marks are silently dropped (F6), unknown roles become bare `div` and `custom` becomes `role="group"`, and `name`/`description`/`transcript` are never mapped; `alt` is written to `<video>`/`<audio>`/`<a>` where it is not an accessible alternative; `scope` tokens are wrong (F17). Restore: `aria-label` is destroyed rather than restored, `data-auy-root` is deleted, `lang`/`dir` can go stale across `dispatch`, and `innerHTML` re-parsing does not restore node identity/listeners (F7). So it neither preserves the tree fully nor restores exactly.

3) TS/PHP reimplementing core semantics: TS yes, PHP no (except the documented envelope header). `@rich-editor-auy/schema` hardcodes a divergent node list and is never sent to Rust; every WASM entry point hardcodes `Schema::basic()`; `Document.fromEnvelope` reimplements envelope parsing and re-serialization in JS and ignores `format`/`version`/`schema_fingerprint` (F2/F4). PHP only re-implements the header check that plan/09 §4.1 explicitly assigns to `Envelope`; it does not implement schema, steps, normalization or fingerprinting.

4) PHP bytes/envelopes: yes, `fromBytes($bytes)->bytes() === $bytes` holds by construction and by `DocumentTest`, and `format`/`version`/64-hex `schema_fingerprint` are rejected with a typed `InvalidArgumentException`; `requireCompatible` compares fingerprints. Caveats: the documented `Validator::validate($doc->bytes())` path always fails because the CLI rejects envelopes (F3); `withSchema` doesn't exist (F10); PHPStan max will reject the untyped array declarations (F11); `composer`/`php` are unavailable here so those gates were not executed.

5) CLI/examples vs documented API: the CLI implements `validate`/`format`/`diff` (plus `a11y`/`a11y-tree`) and prints `code`/`offset`/`path` on invalid docs, matching plan/08 F3.5; but it accepts only bare docs (F3) and has no schema input (F10). Examples: `examples/ts/main.ts` runs but is not the plan's `mount`/`basicSchema`/`fromEnvelope` quick start; `examples/php/roundtrip.php` matches the implemented `Document` API; the host example imports raw `.ts` and cannot run in a browser (F16); the plan's `Validator(...)->withSchema(...)` sample cannot compile (F10).

6) Publish include gaps: `@rich-editor-auy/core` lists `wasm/*.blake3` but no checksum exists or ships (F14); `@rich-editor-auy/dom` publishes a `deno.json` whose import map points outside the package, making the published module unresolvable (F1); the Rust crates list `LICENSE-MIT`/`LICENSE-APACHE` but package neither (F13). Everything else needed (mod.ts, wasm `.js`/`.d.ts`/`.wasm`, per-package LICENSE) is present in the dry-run manifests; tests are correctly excluded.
